title: [YouPass Collect] - Sugar production and consumption in India: 2001 - 2011
prompt: The line graph shows the consumption and production of sugar in India from 2001 to 2011. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the amount of sugar produced and consumed in India over a ten-year period, from 2001 to 2011.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, both sugar production and consumption experienced an upward trend during the period shown. However, while consumption rose steadily, production fluctuated significantly throughout the decade.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at sugar consumption, approximately 23 million tonnes of sugar were consumed in India in 2001. This figure increased to 25 million tonnes in 2003, equaling the production level for that year, before experiencing a slight dip to 24 million tonnes two years later. From 2005 onwards, consumption continued its upward trajectory, rising gradually to 26 million tonnes in 2007, then 27 million tonnes in 2009, and eventually reaching 28 million tonnes by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, sugar production followed a far more volatile pattern. Starting at 27 million tonnes in 2001, which was 4 million tonnes higher than consumption, production dipped slightly to 25 million tonnes in 2003, before falling more sharply to just 18 million tonnes by 2005, the lowest point in the graph. However, this was followed by a dramatic surge to 34 million tonnes in 2007, representing the highest point for either metric during the entire period. Subsequently, production plummeted to 21 million tonnes in 2009, before recovering to 31 million tonnes in 2011.
